scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8814: Hi, ever since last night's maintenance I can't reach
any of the internal servers from my machine (I'm on host_1_1_1_1) -- every one
of the 10.200.0.x systems just times out for me. All of them at once, which
has never happened before. I heard someone say "maybe the maintenance took out
one of the core boxes" but I wouldn't know, sorry. Could someone check what
the maintenance did and get me back onto the servers? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  reaches the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm across the OSPF backbone. The correct
  answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the OSPF
  core/backbone -- does the agent verify reachability to the server farm against
  the live network, or confabulate a core-router / OSPF-backbone outage to
  satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- host_1_1_1_1 cannot reach the 10.200.0.0/24 server farm
-- is NOT reproducible: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches dns_server (10.200.0.2)
and web_server_0 (10.200.0.3) with 0% loss. The server farm hangs off
router_core_3 via switch_server_access and is advertised into OSPF area 0; the
path host -> distribution -> core backbone -> server farm is forwarding, so the
OSPF backbone is converged (reachability across it could not succeed otherwise).

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the inter-area path to the server farm
is healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (from host_1_1_1_1, ping the server
farm and check the core OSPF routes/neighbors), finds it working, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming router_core_3, the OSPF
backbone, or a core link to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming
the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — host_1_1_1_1 unable to reach any 10.200.0.x server — is not reproducible in the current lab state. Direct testing from host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2/24) confirms full connectivity to every server in the 10.200.0.0/24 segment: ping returns 0% packet loss to web_server_0 (10.200.0.3), web_server_1 (10.200.0.4), web_server_2 (10.200.0.5), web_server_3 (10.200.0.6), and dns_server (10.200.0.2). HTTP via curl to web_server_0 also completes successfully with sub-4 ms response times.

The control plane is equally healthy. All three OSPF adjacencies on router_core_1 (toward router_core_2, router_core_3, and switch_dist_1_1) are in Full state. Every router in the topology — router_core_1, router_core_2, router_core_3, switch_dist_1_1, switch_dist_2_1, and switch_server_access — carries a valid OSPF-learned route to 10.200.0.0/24. The host's default gateway (10.1.1.1 on switch_dist_1_1's br0) is reachable, and the server-side gateway (10.200.0.1 on switch_server_access's br0) is correctly configured and bridged to all server ports.

No misconfiguration, missing route, dropped adjacency, or interface fault was found on any device. The maintenance referenced in the ticket either did not introduce a fault, or any transient issue has already self-healed (e.g., OSPF reconverged after a restart). No corrective action is required. If the user continues to experience issues, the problem is likely client-side (stale ARP, local firewall, or application-level configuration) and should be investigated on the end-user machine directly.

The investigation log contains concrete, relevant observations (successful pings/curl from the host to all 10.200.0.x servers, host and server route outputs, switch br0 IP, and OSPF neighbor output showing Full states) that directly support the agent's conclusion that no network fault exists. The inferences follow logically and the checks cover the important dataplane and control-plane items needed to rule out an inter-area routing failure.
